facts.text: VisFly is a quadrotor simulator for vision-based flight and is built on Habitat-Sim
The demo datasets are built from ReplicaCAD and are downloaded separately from Hugging Face with Git LFS
The modified habitat-sim is cloned separately and built from source
The conda environment pins habitat-sim==0.3.1
NavigationEnv extends DroneGymEnvsBase
DroneGymEnvsBase extends the stable-baselines3 VecEnv
NavigationEnv defaults to seed 42, visual=True and max_episode_steps=256
The action space is a four-element Box with low -1 and high 1 for bodyrate, thrust, velocity and position control
The default action type is bodyrate
The control interval ctrl_dt defaults to 0.03 s and the integration step dt to 0.005 s
The state is position (3), orientation quaternion (4), velocity (3) and angular velocity (3), 13 values in total
The observation space is a Dict whose state Box has state_size elements
NavigationEnv adds a target Box of 3 values to the observation space and the default target is [9, 0, 1]
When visual is true the observation also carries a depth array read from the sensor observations
reset accepts an optional state and returns the observations
The reset state is a four- or six-part tuple: position, orientation, velocity, angular velocity and optionally motor speed and thrust
step requires a reset first, converts the action to a tensor and advances the simulator
An episode is done on success, failure, out of bounds, collision, or when the step count reaches max_episode_steps
collect_info sets TimeLimit.truncated when the step count has reached max_episode_steps
Success means the distance from the position to the target is at most success_radius
The success radius defaults to 0.5
DroneEnvsBase.set_seed forwards the seed to the dynamics and the scene manager
Dynamics.set_seed calls torch.manual_seed
The dynamics constructor seeds itself with its seed argument

determinism.notes: a reset seed is applied through DroneEnvsBase.set_seed, which calls torch.manual_seed and sets the scene-manager seed (envs/base/droneEnv.py:381-385, envs/base/dynamics.py:556-557); the fake reseeds its start-state generator from the same seed. The two use different generators, so one seed repeats a trajectory within one implementation but not across the fake and upstream

gaps: kinematic point model: the four commands are mapped to a velocity vector; there is no rigid-body dynamics, motor, rotor, drag, contact, wind, sensor-noise or scene model (the upstream engine is Habitat-Sim, readme.md:6)
the fake rewards are a placeholder distance term, not the upstream navigation reward (envs/NavigationEnv.py:85-99)

the depth/RGB rendering and the habitat-sim scenes are NOT COVERED: the fake observation has only state (13 values) and target (3 values), while the upstream visual observation adds depth (envs/NavigationEnv.py:69-74); the fake start state is drawn from Python's random generator, upstream draws it from a torch state generator

the sim backend is refused: the upstream simulation needs the modified habitat-sim built from source and the ReplicaCAD demo dataset (readme.md:36-48, readme.md:62-73), neither of which was installed or run
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step, reset or seed is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the world state is kept and stays readable
